description: We are a team of students from the University of Technology and Applied Sciences in Ibra, bringing together expertise from two different fields: Engineering and Information Technology. This project marks our very first participation in NASA Space Apps, and we are driven by a shared ambition to reach our full potential and achieve our ultimate goals through this inspiring experience.
summary: We're the Extra X Link team. This is a brand new, interactive 6 stage global video game which trains children as Junior Astronauts in the design and operation of a fully functional space colony. It directly addresses and solves the key problems with all of the 6 existing space games. It's a real life human survival game (energy, oxygen, food, nutrition, zero waste etc) combined with the actual building of space habitats. To develop problem solving skills we have a dynamic crisis engine which will throw you a crisis at any time (solar flare, micrometeorite hit, critical airlock leak etc). You get points for performance, for speed and for collecting 20 pieces of orbital space debris per stage which you can then trade in for construction materials or emergency hints. It's built on accessible cross platform engines (Unity, Unreal etc) so it's fully accessible to everyone regardless of hardware. It's the solution to the education gap, combining space exploration with STEM in a fun, accessible and language neutral way that will also instill an awareness of the environment and inspire the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Project solution

   

It's an interactive educational game comprising 6 stages in which you build and run a space colony and train up the kids as junior astronauts. The whole concept is to close the educational gap by using space exploration as a vehicle to deliver STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths). It's based on real NASA concepts in terms of the way you manage your oxygen and your energy. There's a crisis engine that will throw you a crisis at any time (solar flares etc) and there's a rewards system for both solving the problems and collecting the space debris.

 

 

 

 

 How does our solution work:

        This project is about closing the educational gap and making space science accessible and interesting to kids. It does this by taking real NASA research and turning it into a six stage interactive video game. The game is built on the principles of gamification and experiential learning in which the player is actively involved in the construction and operation of a full space colony. The game has a dynamic crisis engine which will force the player to use their problem solving and critical thinking skills to deal with all sorts of sudden emergencies (solar flares, micrometeorites etc). It will also teach the player about management and the environment through the need to manage the life support systems (oxygen, water, energy and food) and to collect space debris. There's also an active reward economy which allows the player to earn points which can be traded in for building materials and emergency hints. It's a fully playable game on any device and is completely accessible globally with no technical barriers to entry. The aim is to inspire the next generation to go into STEM.

The main missions teach three ideas:

1. Airlock safety: debris can damage a habitat, and a leak lets air escape.

2.Finding lunar water: the Moon’s sunlight, temperature, and terrain affect where ice may be found.

3. Managing power: a colony must protect life-support systems while balancing limited energy.

The game benefits:

* Educating players on space missions, resource management (life support, energy, water, and food), and structural engineering.

* Demonstrating practical problem-solving and critical thinking strategies through dynamic space crises.

* Bridging the gap between real-world NASA training concepts and accessible, engaging STEM education.

 

Our goal

 

To make space science and astronaut training more accessible, helping children worldwide explore aerospace concepts through a 6-stage interactive simulation game that builds a self-sustaining space colony.

Coding languages:

*c#---->for 2D game development

Tools, languages, and hardware

We built Space Colony Academy in Unity 6.6 using C#, Unity UI, and TextMeshPro. We exported it for WebGL so it can be played in a browser, and are using Unity Play to share it. Development used a standard Windows computer; players can use a keyboard and mouse, with no special hardware required. OpenAI Codex assisted with coding, debugging, and documentation.

Creativity and design considerations

The game’s creative hook is “follow the evidence, then repair the colony.” Players investigate clues, choose an action, see an immediate result, and get a short science explanation. Three missions turn airlock repair, lunar ice prospecting, and power management into interactive challenges for young learners.

We considered age-appropriate language, simple controls, browser accessibility, and a manageable project scope. NASA DONKI and NOAA GOES data provide space-weather context; NASA lunar research informs the ice mission. Mission outcomes and resource changes are simplified game simulations, not real measurements of conditions at a lunar colony.
